title: MLA shared latent with sparse private KV residual
hypothesis: Shared latent Mirror reconstruction plus sparse private KV residual preserves attention-output quality across heterogeneous roles at lower cache bytes than independent KV states.
mirror_coordinate: head x layer latent code with sparse role-private K/V residual

development.selection_metric: attention output nMSE vs actual serialized bytes

fresh.reason: Direct coefficients exactly match shared latent code; frozen byte/quality gate uses development.

success_gate: Attention-output nMSE <=1e-3 at <=25% private fraction, >=20% fewer bytes than independent cache at heterogeneity <=0.3, and Mirror-specific advantage over direct coefficients.
failure_gate: Private state erases byte savings or direct coefficients match Mirror.
boundaries: no real MLA kernel or LM claim
